title: App Connector provisioning keys
aliases: view or export provisioning key after creation

prose.text: A provisioning key is one of the two ways to enroll a connector; this subject covers what the key is and how it is consumed.

prose.label: Use limits.
prose.text: {{max-reuse}} {{exhausted-key-blocks-deploy}} {{multiple-keys-per-group}} Whether moving a connector between groups needs a new key is not stated {{gap:cross-group-move}}.

prose.label: When enrollment fails on the key.
prose.text: {{mcp-skill-key-issues-first}} {{mcp-skill-exhaustion-test}} {{incorrect-copy-error}} What an exhausted key looks like on the connector, and whether copied whitespace breaks a key, are not sourced {{gap:exhausted-key-symptom}} {{gap:trailing-whitespace}}.

How the SDKs and the MCP server model keys is in [[zpa.app-connectors.provisioning-key-tooling]]; association types and provider lookups are in [[zpa.sdk-go.service-defects]]; the `enabled = false` write is in [[shared.sdk-go.zero-value-writes]]. The wider enrollment sequence is in [[zpa.app-connectors.enrollment]].

checks.do: The key's maximum and utilization count, before blaming the connector for a failed enrollment.
Whether the connector console shows the 401 enrollment failure that the help attributes to an incorrectly copied key.
Whether the key column is blank because the View or Export option was disabled, which makes the key unrecoverable.
Whether the key is Deception-configured or Zscaler-managed before planning to edit or delete it.

key-enrolls-connector.statement: A provisioning key is a text string that enrolls an App Connector; it works as the connector's credential, letting the Private Access cloud verify the connector and complete deployment.

quotes: The provisioning key is a text string that is used to enroll an App Connector.
The provisioning key functions like a credential for the App Connector, enabling the Private Access (ZPA) cloud to verify the App Connector's authenticity and complete the deployment process.

key-names-group.statement: Each key is associated with a specific App Connector group, so the key tells the Private Access cloud which group a connector is deployed into.

quotes: each key is associated with a specific App Connector group, so the key allows the Private Access cloud to identify the App Connector group to which an App Connector must be deployed.

key-is-secret.statement: Provisioning keys should be treated as secrets because they can create a resource for a tenant, and must not be transmitted or stored in clear text.

quotes: Provisioning keys should be treated as secrets and properly protected because they can create a resource for a tenant.
The provisioning key must also be secured and not transmitted or stored in clear text.

key-format-example.statement: The help's example key is pipe-separated: a leading number, the API host api.private.zscaler.com, then a long base64 payload. The enrollment error output shows the same host in its nonce.

quotes: 1|api.private.zscaler.com|68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ
error:Login request failed - http status(401) nonce(<3|api.private.zscaler.com|0/Z6lDT...>)

key-format-example.conditions: Reads the field layout from one example key and one error line; the help does not define the fields.

max-reuse.statement: A key can be limited to a number of uses when it is generated (Maximum Reuse of Provisioning Key), and Private Access tracks the count and shows it as the Provisioning Key Utilization Count.

quotes: When you generate a provisioning key, you can specify the number of times a key can be used to deploy App Connectors.
Private Access tracks the number of times a key is used to deploy an App Connector and displays it on the App Connector Provisioning Keys page.
Provisioning Key Utilization Count: The number of times the provisioning key has been used.

exhausted-key-blocks-deploy.statement: When a key has been used its maximum number of times it cannot deploy more App Connectors, but its maximum can always be edited. The Copy icon is disabled with a Warning icon at that point.

quotes: When a key is used the maximum number of times, you cannot use it to deploy more App Connectors. However, you can always edit the maximum number of times a key can be used.
If the Provisioning Key Utilization Count is reached, you cannot copy the key. A Warning icon appears next to the disabled Copy icon. You can edit the key to raise the limit.

multiple-keys-per-group.statement: Several provisioning keys can be associated with one App Connector group.

quotes: You also have the option of associating multiple provisioning keys to a single App Connector group.

key-hidden-after-creation.statement: If View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation was disabled, the key column is blank and the copy and download icons are hidden. Unless a backup is in an external credential vault, a new key must be generated, and it can be attached to the same App Connector.

quotes: This entry is blank if you disabled the View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation option when configuring App Connector groups.

If the provisioning key doesn't appear, and a backup of the provisioning key isn't securely stored in an external credential vault, a new key must be generated. A new provisioning key can be created and attached to the same App Connector.
Copy the provisioning key to your clipboard.
If you disabled the View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation option when configuring an App Connector group, this icon is hidden for security purposes.
Download the provisioning key to your system in a file format.
If you disabled the View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation option when configuring an App Connector, this icon is hidden for security purposes.

incorrect-copy-error.statement: A key that was copied incorrectly shows up in the App Connector console as an enrollment attempt ending in a 401 login failure and Certificate enrollment failed.

quotes: When a provisioning key is incorrectly copied, the following error appears in your App Connector console when it tries to enroll:
error:Login request failed - http status(401)
notice:Certificate enrollment failed.

deception-managed-read-only.statement: A provisioning key configured with Zscaler Deception, or managed by Zscaler, has its edit and delete options unavailable.

quotes: If a provisioning key is configured using Zscaler Deception or is managed by Zscaler, then the edit and delete options are unavailable.

key-selects-signing-cert.statement: A provisioning key lets the admin select the signing certificate used to enroll App Connector certificates.

quotes: Select the signing certificate used to enroll App Connector certificates.

mcp-skill-key-issues-first.statement: The MCP server's connector troubleshooting skill calls provisioning key issues the leading cause of enrollment failure and lists three: max_usage reached, a key copied incorrectly, and a key associated with the wrong connector group.

quotes: Provisioning key issues are the #1 cause of enrollment failures.
Key max_usage reached (Step 3 above)
Key copied incorrectly -- administrator should re-copy the exact key
Key associated with wrong connector group

mcp-skill-exhaustion-test.statement: The same skill tests exhaustion by comparing the key's max_usage with its current enrollment count: if equal, no new enrollments can use the key. A ZMS skill in the same repository writes the test as usageCount >= maxUsage.

quotes: max_usage` vs current enrollment count -- if equal, no new enrollments can use this key
usageCount >= maxUsage

mcp-skill-exhaustion-test.conditions: The ZMS skill covers a different product's keys; it is cited only for how the same predicate is phrased.

exhausted-key-symptom.title: Symptom of an exhausted key
exhausted-key-symptom.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Symptoms: new App Connector instances fail to enroll; old ones keep working." and "A literal copy of this error in a support ticket narrows diagnosis to 'key is wrong, truncated, or utilization-exhausted.'" The help ties the 401 error only to an incorrectly copied key and says an exhausted key cannot be used or copied; it does not show what an enrolling connector logs for an exhausted key.

trailing-whitespace.title: Whitespace in a copied provisioning key
trailing-whitespace.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Provisioning keys copied from the portal UI can silently include trailing whitespace. Operators pasting the key into a deployment template should trim whitespace; the notice:Login request failed - http status(401) error in the error log is the giveaway." No source states that the portal copy adds whitespace.

cross-group-move.title: Moving a connector between groups
cross-group-move.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Cross-group moves require re-enrollment with a different key." The help says a key identifies the group a connector is deployed into and that a deployed connector is replaced by deleting and re-enrolling it (see enrollment); it does not say that moving between groups requires a new key.
